examples.knowledge_point: Computing the One-Sided Limits of a Piecewise Function when the Limits Do Not Coincide
examples.problem:
Find the left-sided and right-sided limits at $x=0$ for the function

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x)={\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}+3\, & \text{ for }\,x<0 \\ \sqrt{x}\, & \text{ for }\,x\ge 0.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
Approaching from the left, we have $x < 0,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=-x^2+3.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}(-{x}^{2}+3) \\  & =-(0)^{2}+3 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Approaching from the right, we have $x>0,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=\sqrt{x}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\sqrt{x} \\  & =\sqrt{0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the left-sided limit at $x=2$ of the piecewise function $f(x)$ defined by

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-x-2 & \text{ for }\,x<2 \\ -{x}^{2}+6x-8 & \text{ for }\,x\ge 2.\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Approaching from the left, we have $x<2,$ so we use the expression $f(x)={x}^{2}-x-2.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{-}}{x}^{2}-x-2 \\  & =(2)^{2}-2-2 \\  & =4-2-2 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
